title.value: Turn tickets into merged pull requests

introduction.value: Pulls tasks from GitHub Issues or Linear, then runs Claude Code or Codex in isolated Kubernetes pods to carry each one through to a PR.

method.value: Optio is a self-hosted tool you run on Kubernetes. You assign it a GitHub Issue, Linear ticket or Jira card. It finds or creates a long-lived pod for the repo and adds a git worktree. It runs the agent there and opens a PR. A PR watcher polls CI and review state, and resumes the agent with context on CI failures, merge conflicts or review feedback. A review agent also runs.

outcome.value: The README says the pipeline runs end to end, squash-merging when CI is green and the review is done, then closing the linked issue and recording cost. It gives no success rates or benchmark numbers.

notes.value: It needs Kubernetes v1.33 or newer, Helm, Postgres and Redis. Auto-resumes are capped by the OPTIO_MAX_AUTO_RESUMES setting, so stuck PRs can still need a person.

source_text.body:
Turn tickets into merged pull requests
Pulls tasks from GitHub Issues or Linear, then runs Claude Code or Codex in isolated Kubernetes pods to carry each one through to a PR.
Done with
CC
Claude Code
CX
Codex
What they did
Optio is a self-hosted tool you run on Kubernetes. You assign it a GitHub Issue, Linear ticket or Jira card. It finds or creates a long-lived pod for the repo and adds a git worktree. It runs the agent there and opens a PR. A PR watcher polls CI and review state, and resumes the agent with context on CI failures, merge conflicts or review feedback. A review agent also runs.
How it went
The README says the pipeline runs end to end, squash-merging when CI is green and the review is done, then closing the linked issue and recording cost. It gives no success rates or benchmark numbers.
Worth knowing
It needs Kubernetes v1.33 or newer, Helm, Postgres and Redis. Auto-resumes are capped by the OPTIO_MAX_AUTO_RESUMES setting, so stuck PRs can still need a person.
Try it yourself
with
Codex
Copy prompt
Look at the open issues in my repo [owner/repo] labeled [label, e.g. good-first-issue] and pick the [number, e.g. 3] smallest ones. For each, work on its own branch, make the fix, run the tests, and prepare a draft pull request description. Pause and show me each diff and PR description before you push anything or open a PR.
Original source: https://github.com/jonwiggins/optio
